title: Taiwan’s Delta Electronics warns power shortages could constrain AI growth
key_facts: Delta Electronics Chair Cheng Ping said on Thursday (15 Oct) that power infrastructure is not keeping pace with AI data center growth.
Four major US cloud providers are expected to spend 4.7 times as much on capital spending this year as in 2022, while power-system investment grew 1.8-fold.
Citing estimates, US data centers are expected to add 44 GW of demand by 2028 while the grid adds only 25 GW, a 19 GW gap.
Data center electricity use could triple from last year's level by 2030, he said.
Delta is investing in solid oxide fuel cells and solid-state transformers; its prefabricated power product can cut on-site deployment time by 50%.
quote_evidence: Delta Electronics Chair Cheng Ping said Thursday that power infrastructure is failing to keep pace with the rapid expansion of AI data centers.
Citing estimates, Cheng said US data centers are expected to add 44 GW of electricity demand by 2028, while the power grid is projected to add only 25 GW in supply capacity, leaving a 19 GW gap.
why_it_matters_hint: A power equipment maker, which sells the fix, warns that electricity could limit AI growth.
notes: Delta sells power equipment, so the warning is from an interested party; figures are estimates he cited.
